summary: This dataset was created using the referenced code at 10.5281/zenodo.24158671 . For more information on how this dataset can be generated, consult the README.md that is found there. The results are presented in 'Titz et al., Cascading failures and system splits in decarbonized European power systems, Joule (2026), DOI:  10.1016/j.joule.2026.102742 '. In this work, we assess the risk of cascading failures and system splits in the European power grid for different carbon reduction scenarios. We analyze the most likely and most dangerous splits, identify critical transmission infrastructures and characteristic split patterns, and we discuss potential countermeasures that can address the problem of cascades. Our results show that while the risk of splits causing power failures rises with decarbonization, it can be mitigated cost-efficiently.
title: Data accompanying 'Cascading failures and system splits in decarbonized European power systems'

summary: Overview The integration of inverter-based renewable energy sources into electric grids challenges conventional power system protection. Machine learning-based solutions can address these challenges by utilizing available data in modern smart grids. However, the lack of open datasets prevents reproducibility and fair comparisons between different approaches and their results, which hinders further progress. Therefore, we propose EvEMTBench, a synthetic dataset of faults and events generated using electromagnetic transient simulations. The physical plausibility of the power system simulation is ensured by validating the simulation parameters against established literature and providing a comprehensive documentation of the simulation procedure. The dataset is designed for training, fine-tuning, and benchmarking machine learning models by providing synchronized point-on-wave voltage and current measurements at 9600 Hz across a diverse set of topologies and voltage levels. The inclusion of a wide range of fault and operating events allows the utilization of EvEMTBench for different tasks like incipient fault detection, fault localization or event detection. The dataset is available on FAUDataCloud and the generation code is available on GitHub as well as this repository on Zenodo. Usage Guide This repository contains the code to generate the dataset. It was tested with Python 3.9 and PowerFactory 2025. The main entry point is "main_datagen.py" - this script orchestrates the dataset generation pipeline. "create_datasets.py" provides higher-level dataset creation functionality. Please refer to the readme.md file for further instructions on how to execute the code to generate custom versions of the dataset. Use Cases The dataset can be used for a wide range of power system protection related tasks, including fault detection, fault classification, fault line indentification, fault localization and fault area classification. Additionally, the dataset can be used for broader tasks like event classification and localization or incipient fault detection.
title: EvEMTBench, a simulation based dataset of faults and events for machine learning in power systems: Code for Data Generation

The inclusion of a wide range of fault and operating events allows the utilization of EvEMTBench for different tasks like incipient fault detection, fault localization or event detection. The dataset is available on FAUDataCloud and the generation code is available on GitHub as well as this repository on Zenodo. Usage Guide This repository contains the code to generate the dataset. It was tested with Python 3.9 and PowerFactory 2025. The main entry point is "main_datagen.py" - this script orchestrates the dataset generation pipeline. "create_datasets.py" provides higher-level dataset creation functionality. Please refer to the readme.md file for further instructions on how to execute the code to generate custom versions of the dataset. Use Cases The dataset can be used for a wide range of power system protection related tasks, including fault detection, fault classification, fault line indentification, fault localization and fault area classification. Additionally, the dataset can be used for broader tasks like event classification and localization or incipient fault detection.
title: EvEMTBench, a simulation based dataset of faults and events for machine learning in power systems: Code for Data Generation

summary: Data belonging to the work "An architectural upgrade? Funiculus hypertrophy under altered source–sink balance in Lunaria annua" Using Lunaria annua , I manipulated resource availability via branch removal to test whether reduced competition induces compensatory funiculus thickening. I measured funiculus thickness and seed area in basal and apical fruits, analyzing seed fate and trait scaling relationships. Branch removal induced global funiculus hypertrophy, which was disproportionately higher in basal positions. Funiculus expansion was positively associated with seed survival and growth, though plants converted transport capacity into biomass more effectively in apical positions. Results also showed a decoupling of the within-fruit size–number trade-off, challenging classical inverse correlations.
tags: competition, plasticity, resource allocation, seed abortion, sub-individual variation.
title: An architectural upgrade? Funiculus hypertrophy under altered source–sink balance in Lunaria annua

summary: The rapid growth of digital payments has increased the importance of reliable credit card fraud detection systems. Traditional rule-based approaches can struggle to identify com plex and evolving fraud patterns, particularly when fraudulent transactions represent only a small proportion of transaction data. This paper presents a machine learning-based framework that combines data preprocessing, class-imbalance handling, autoencoder-based feature representation, and XGBoost clas sification. The study uses the publicly available credit card transaction dataset containing 284,807 transactions, including 492 fraudulent transactions. Robust scaling is used to reduce the influence of extreme values, while the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) is applied only to the training data. An autoencoder learns a compact representation of trans action features and calculates reconstruction error; these outputs are combined with the prepared features for downstream clas sification. XGBoost is used to distinguish legitimate transactions from potentially fraudulent ones. The framework is evaluated using precision, recall, F1-score, area under the precision recall curve (PR-AUC), and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). The paper also describes an API-oriented deployment workflow. Numerical results should be reported from the final reproducible experiment; illustrative or previously obtained values must not be treated as independently verified without rerunning the implementation.
title: Securing Digital Transactions: Machine Learning for Credit Card Fraud Detection

summary: Equipment-embodied growth theory predicts that reallocating fixed-capital formation from civil structures toward machinery and plant modernization accelerates industrial output, yet high-investment transition regions routinely channel over half of capital outlays into construction-installation works. Assembling regional fixed-capital simplex panels across all 14 regions of Uzbekistan (2000–2025 for technological shares, N = 364; 2007–2025 for reproduction modes, N = 266; 2016–2025 for constant-price industrial value-added growth, N = 140) alongside boundary-harmonized regional benchmarks from Kazakhstan (2003–2026Q3), we evaluate compositional reallocation hypotheses using full-simplex two-way fixed-effects regressions and 9,999 null-imposed wild cluster bootstrap replications. Across all six primary specifications conditioning on real investment scale, real investment growth, employment growth, and residual simplex shares, shifting 10 percentage points from construction-installation works into machinery and equipment yields statistically unresolved contemporaneous (+0.74 percentage points; bootstrap p = 0.7025; 95% bootstrap interval [-1.66, 3.66]) and lagged (+0.56; bootstrap p = 0.3828) industrial growth associations that remain null under predetermined scale controls (+0.63; bootstrap p = 0.3710); a one-year-ahead dynamic association (+1.52; bootstrap p = 0.0319) does not survive six-horizon Holm correction (p = 0.1914), and omitting either Karakalpakstan's 10 region-years (-0.60; bootstrap p = 0.0812) or its single 2016 observation (-0.35; bootstrap p = 0.4017) reverses contemporaneous point estimates negative. On the capital-input margin, reallocating 10 percentage points from greenfield expansion to reconstruction and modernization is associated with a 4.35 percentage-point higher regional machinery share (bootstrap p = 0.0003; 5.75 percentage points with real-scale controls, bootstrap p = 0.0003), while Uzbek-Kazakh subnational comparisons show persistent civil-works dominance whose cross-sectional financing gradients depend on regional consolidation and own-funds scope. summary: A tape of n cells over three values — equivalently, two-bit cells read through their sum — is read by two headers that enclose a window; at each step a fixed rule, given the window's content and the geometry, names one of eight actions: move a header inward or outward, trim a cell from the left, the right or both, or halt. The cost is the number of cell reads, the state is O(log n) bits, and the question is how the cost must grow with n for each rule. The rules fall into three classes — fully linear, semi-linear and superlinear — separated by a worst-case cost and a mean cost. All three are populated: five natural rules are fully linear, one construction is semi-linear, and the remaining sixteen are superlinear.   The paper separates the walk from the cells it reads, proves that the collapse of the group-sum rules costs n + S - 1 reads in six lines, shows that one machine is within a constant of all three optima even when they are attained by different machines, arranges the catalogue's costs on a ladder from n^{1/2} to n^3, and states exactly what is proved, what is measured and what is open. It carries one conjecture: that no content-dependent rule can be superlinear and perfect. Negative results included: the certificate bound does not compose (on one tape the per-query certificates sum to 1,285,703 cells while their union has 1,020), and a bound on the rule's output transfers to the walk only after multiplication by the fraction of queries at which the answer can change the action, measured at 0.104 and falling like n^{-0.99}.   This version replaces the earlier one: the classification is three-class throughout, four conjectures of the earlier draft are gone, the collapse is a theorem rather than a numerical check, and the machine profile of Appendix A reports for every rule the three minima and the machine that attains each.
title: A memoryless two-header tape machine: what a window costs, and why two lower-bound techniques fail

summary: FAIR metadata (Schema.org, Bioschemas and MLCommons Croissant) for the ELIXIR 3D-BioInfo benchmark of 1,677 homodimer interfaces from 1,645 protein crystal structures, together with the structure files (PDB and mmCIF), an in-repository snapshot of the PDB metadata of every entry, and the documentation of the label curation. The benchmark was published by Schweke et al. (2023, Proteomics 23(17):e2200323, doi:10.1002/pmic.202200323; 836 physiological and 841 non-physiological interfaces). This package uses the curated annotation file of the benchmark authors (844 physiological and 833 non-physiological interfaces; 16 labels revised, 20 interfaces flagged ambiguous and 6 flagged for deletion). Every interface carries both the curated label and the published label ( PublishedPhysio ). See data/curation/README.md . Please cite the original publication as well as this package.

summary: # Reported suspected cholera in Nigeria, 2022–2024 **NCDC-derived state and highest-burden LGA data, analysis code and results (version 1.0.0)** Companion deposit for: Okonkwo CO, Adejumo AO. *Shifting geography of reported suspected cholera in Nigeria, 2022–2024: a surveillance analysis of state and highest-burden local government area reports.* [Journal / DOI to be added.] Licence: CC BY 4.0. Cite this deposit by its Zenodo DOI: [to be assigned]. Source reports: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, https://ncdc.gov.ng; reports were abstracted in November 2026 (URLs are in the `source_url` column of each data file). ## 1. What is in this deposit | Folder / file | Contents | |---|---| | `data/ncdc_cholera_top_lgas_published.csv` | Highest-burden LGA tables: epidemiological week 52 of 2022 and 2023, week 39 of 2024. 43 rows (15, 14, 14), 42 distinct LGAs. Columns: year, period_covered, rank, lga, state, cases, source, source_url. | | `data/ncdc_cholera_state_by_year.csv` | Suspected cases and deaths for each state listed in the situation reports (33, 31 and 36 states). Columns include as_of, status, source_url. | | `data/ncdc_cholera_national_published.csv` | National totals at each reporting point: suspected and confirmed cases, deaths, CFR, states and LGAs affected, including the full-year 2024 figure (24,842 suspected cases) from the Weekly Epidemiological Report, vol. 14, no. 52. | | `data/state_input_data_populations_coordinates.csv` | Analysis input: 2006 census population, area, state centroid (mean of LGA coordinates), cases, listed flags. | | `data/lga_coordinates_and_zones.csv` | 774 LGAs with state, geopolitical zone and coordinates. Used only to compute state centroids. Contains no case counts. | | `code/state_analysis_v2.py` | State-level analyses (Moran's I, LISA, rank correlation, Bayesian BYM2 negative binomial models, posterior predictive checks, WAIC, NB regression) and Figures 3–4 inputs. | | `code/lga_extra.py` | Table of all listed LGAs and the random-selection overlap simulation (200,000 draws; fixed seed). | | `code/analysis_top_lgas.py` | Descriptive, concentration and overlap analysis of the published LGA lists. | | `code/maps.py` | State symbol maps (Figure 2). | | `results/` | All output tables and JSON. Prefix `state_` = state-level analyses; `lga_` = LGA-list analyses. | | `figures/` | PNG figures. | | `supplement/` | Supplementary File 1 (STROBE/RECORD checklist), 2 (search protocol and reference verification log), 3 (supplementary tables), and `Supplementary_Tables.xlsx`. | | `MANIFEST_SHA256.txt` | SHA-256 checksum of every file. | ## 2. Key definitions and handling of data - **Suspected cholera:** cases as published by NCDC under its suspected-case definition; not laboratory-confirmed. - **Incidence:** reported suspected cases per 100,000 of the 2006 census population (reported, not true, incidence). - **2024:** epidemiological weeks 1–39 (10,837 suspected cases). The state and LGA tables for 2024 end at week 39. - **Unlisted states:** a state absent from an NCDC table is either unaffected or did not report; these cannot be distinguished. Primary analyses treat them as **missing**; sensitivity analyses treat them as zero. summary: FAIR metadata, query tool and web portal for the benchmark experiment 1 (BE1) of the ELIXIR Single Cell Omics community: a 10x Genomics single-cell RNA-seq experiment with seven lung cancer cell lines carrying different driver alterations (EGFR, KRAS, MET, BRAF, ERBB2, ROS1, ALK) and a PBMC population (GEO series GSE243665; 29,128 cells from the cell lines and 478 PBMC). The experiment is described with the Single Cell Schema version 0.4 ( scrna-schema/ ) and linked to the public records of GEO, SRA, BioProject and figshare. The count data are not part of this repository; they are available from GEO and figshare. The experiment was published by Arigoni et al. (2024, Scientific Data 11:159, doi:10.1038/s41597-024-03002-y). Please cite the original publication as well as this package.

summary: Replication package for  Neuro-Symbolic Requirements Elicitation: Utilizing Formal Verification Counterexamples as Contextual Prompts  (ASE 2026). C-GRiD combines a Large Language Model (LLM) with the TLA+ model checker TLC. Counterexamples are translated into plain-language questions for stakeholders, whose answers guide the iterative refinement of formal specifications. Version 2.0.0 provides a new experimental evaluation of C-GRiD that replaces the evaluation of Version 1 , with an executable and reproducible evaluation pipeline. The results reported in this version supersede those of Version 1. In particular, Version 2 introduces the following enhancements: TLC-based verification:  All experimental verdicts are established using the TLC model checker (TLC2 2026.11.06, bundled with the package). Executable benchmarks:  The nine benchmarks are provided as executable TLA+ models with their corresponding TLC configuration files, while preserving the constraint identifiers used in Version 1. Behavioural recall assessment:  Recall is determined through TLC refinement checks, providing an executable basis for assessing whether the specified requirements are satisfied. Complete experimental traceability:  Every LLM interaction is recorded, allowing the reported results to be re-derived without requiring an API key through  replay.sh . Experimental Evaluation Version 2 reports a new experimental evaluation using two LLM configurations: Claude Sonnet 5.5 ( claude-sonnet-5-5 , answering through a manual queue). Qwen3.6-27B (self-hosted server, temperature 0.3). The experimental setting comprises nine benchmarks, k = 3 and 5 removed constraints, five seeds, and 90 cases per approach and LLM. Strict Recall Results Approach Claude Sonnet 5.5 Qwen3.6-27B C-GRiD, perfect stakeholder 91.9% 89.6% C-GRiD, noisy stakeholder 85.4% 80.4% Gen-Once, full requirements 92.2% 59.1% Gen-Once, missing requirements hidden 83.3% 66.5% Auto-Repair (no LLM) 81.3% 81.3% Pairwise Comparisons C-GRiD with a perfect stakeholder compared with the other approaches (paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test): C-GRiD vs. Claude Sonnet 5.5 Qwen3.6-27B Auto-Repair +10.6 pp, p = 0.0005 +8.3 pp, p = 0.020 C-GRiD, noisy stakeholder +6.5 pp, p = 0.003 +9.3 pp, p = 0.001 Gen-Once, missing requirements hidden +8.5 pp, p = 0.053 +23.1 pp, p < 0.001 Gen-Once, full requirements −0.4 pp, p = 0.59 +30.6 pp, p < 0.001 The evaluation shows that C-GRiD consistently outperforms Auto-Repair across both LLM configurations. Its comparison with one-shot generation also highlights the influence of the underlying LLM: C-GRiD achieves a substantial advantage with Qwen3.6-27B, whereas Claude Sonnet 5.5 achieves comparable strict recall when provided with the full requirements. These results provide further insight into the conditions under which counterexample-guided elicitation is beneficial. They supersede the results of Version 1 and are not directly comparable with them. They should be interpreted within the experimental setting and limitations documented in  RESULTS.md . Package Contents cgrid/ : C-GRiD implementation and experimental pipeline. benchmarks/ : Nine executable TLA+ benchmarks. results/ : Recorded experimental runs for both LLM configurations. legacy/ : Version 1 package, preserved for reference and comparison. Tests and supporting scripts: replay.sh : Re-derives the reported results from recorded LLM interactions, without requiring an API key. reproduce.sh : Runs new experiments using an LLM endpoint. Requirements:  Python ≥ 3.10 and Java ≥ 11. The package is intended to support independent inspection, replication, and further experimentation with counterexample-guided requirements elicitation.
title: Counterexample-Guided Requirements Discovery

summary: Abstract (it) Il corpus in esame decostruisce il mito dell'applicazione standardizzata della prospettiva albertiana a base quadrata nell'opera di Leonardo da Vinci, proponendo un paradigma metrico-modulare fondato su evidenze geometriche oggettive e falsificabili. Attraverso l'analisi tridimensionale dell'Annunciazione, dell'Adorazione dei Magi e dell'Ultima Cena, emerge una grammatica spaziale in costante evoluzione. Leonardo abbandona la rigida scacchiera per sviluppare un sistema di "righelli inseriti", evolvendo da una misurazione monodirezionale a un'architettura ritmica e stereometrica. Il metodo d'indagine, basato su tecniche di retro-ingegneria CAD e sul "banale aristotelico", dimostra come le proporzioni spaziali (dal modulo 4:3 ai ritmi polifonici 1:4:1 e 2:1:2) siano direttamente ricavabili dall'opera stessa. L'approccio restituisce spazi non solo misurabili, ma architettonicamente rimontabili e strutturati sulle misure umane, rigettando interpretazioni esoteriche o simbologie forzate. Abstract (en) The examined corpus deconstructs the myth of the standardized application of Albertian square-based perspective in the works of Leonardo da Vinci, proposing a metric-modular paradigm founded on objective and falsifiable geometric evidence. Through the three-dimensional analysis of the Annunciation, the Adoration of the Magi, and the Last Supper, a constantly evolving spatial grammar emerges. Leonardo abandons the rigid checkerboard to develop a system of "inserted rulers," evolving from a monodirectional measurement to a rhythmic and stereometric architecture. The investigative method, based on CAD reverse-engineering techniques and the "Aristotelian obvious," demonstrates how spatial proportions (from the 4:3 module to the 1:4:1 and 2:1:2 polyphonic rhythms) can be directly derived from the artwork itself. This approach yields spaces that are not only measurable but architecturally reassemblable and structured on human measurements, rejecting esoteric interpretations or forced symbolism.   Abstract esteso (IT) Il corpus Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score propone una rilettura unitaria di tre indagini nate separatamente ma convergenti verso una stessa ipotesi: Leonardo da Vinci non applica in modo meccanico la prospettiva albertiana a maglia quadrata, né se ne discosta episodicamente per errore o licenza, ma sviluppa progressivamente una propria grammatica spaziale metrico-modulare, verificabile a partire dall'immagine stessa. L'oggetto della ricerca non è una lettura iconografica complessiva delle opere, bensì la ricostruzione degli spazi dipinti come dispositivi misurabili, abitabili e rimontabili attraverso procedure geometriche esplicite. Il trittico mette in relazione tre momenti distinti di questa elaborazione: l’ Annunciazione come forma prototipica della “geometria inserita”, l’ Adorazione dei Magi come emersione di una griglia generativa 4:3 connessa al braccio fiorentino, e l’ Ultima Cena come approdo a una vera polifonia stereometrica, governata da un unico modulo capace di coordinare larghezza, altezza e profondità. In questa prospettiva, lo sviluppo dell’opera leonardesca appare come una sequenza coerente: da uno spazio ancora concentrato e leggibile attraverso pochi regoli incorporati, a un’architettura figurata sempre più complessa, immersiva e ritmica. Sul piano metodologico, il corpus assume come principio guida il “banale aristotelico”: partire esclusivamente da ciò che nel dipinto è visibile, misurabile e geometricamente controllabile, senza ricorrere a simbologie arbitrarie, geometrie occulte o sovrastrutture interpretative non falsificabili. Il metodo combina osservazione diretta delle tracce figurative, geometria inversa, retro-ingegneria CAD e verifiche di coerenza antropometrica, zoometrica e architettonica; il punto decisivo è che gli elementi pittorici — bugne

Attraverso l'analisi tridimensionale dell'Annunciazione, dell'Adorazione dei Magi e dell'Ultima Cena, emerge una grammatica spaziale in costante evoluzione. Leonardo abbandona la rigida scacchiera per sviluppare un sistema di "righelli inseriti", evolvendo da una misurazione monodirezionale a un'architettura ritmica e stereometrica. Il metodo d'indagine, basato su tecniche di retro-ingegneria CAD e sul "banale aristotelico", dimostra come le proporzioni spaziali (dal modulo 4:3 ai ritmi polifonici 1:4:1 e 2:1:2) siano direttamente ricavabili dall'opera stessa. L'approccio restituisce spazi non solo misurabili, ma architettonicamente rimontabili e strutturati sulle misure umane, rigettando interpretazioni esoteriche o simbologie forzate. Abstract (en) The examined corpus deconstructs the myth of the standardized application of Albertian square-based perspective in the works of Leonardo da Vinci, proposing a metric-modular paradigm founded on objective and falsifiable geometric evidence. Through the three-dimensional analysis of the Annunciation, the Adoration of the Magi, and the Last Supper, a constantly evolving spatial grammar emerges. Leonardo abandons the rigid checkerboard to develop a system of "inserted rulers," evolving from a monodirectional measurement to a rhythmic and stereometric architecture. The investigative method, based on CAD reverse-engineering techniques and the "Aristotelian obvious," demonstrates how spatial proportions (from the 4:3 module to the 1:4:1 and 2:1:2 polyphonic rhythms) can be directly derived from the artwork itself. This approach yields spaces that are not only measurable but architecturally reassemblable and structured on human measurements, rejecting esoteric interpretations or forced symbolism.   Abstract esteso (IT) Il corpus Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score propone una rilettura unitaria di tre indagini nate separatamente ma convergenti verso una stessa ipotesi: Leonardo da Vinci non applica in modo meccanico la prospettiva albertiana a maglia quadrata, né se ne discosta episodicamente per errore o licenza, ma sviluppa progressivamente una propria grammatica spaziale metrico-modulare, verificabile a partire dall'immagine stessa. L'oggetto della ricerca non è una lettura iconografica complessiva delle opere, bensì la ricostruzione degli spazi dipinti come dispositivi misurabili, abitabili e rimontabili attraverso procedure geometriche esplicite. Il trittico mette in relazione tre momenti distinti di questa elaborazione: l’ Annunciazione come forma prototipica della “geometria inserita”, l’ Adorazione dei Magi come emersione di una griglia generativa 4:3 connessa al braccio fiorentino, e l’ Ultima Cena come approdo a una vera polifonia stereometrica, governata da un unico modulo capace di coordinare larghezza, altezza e profondità. In questa prospettiva, lo sviluppo dell’opera leonardesca appare come una sequenza coerente: da uno spazio ancora concentrato e leggibile attraverso pochi regoli incorporati, a un’architettura figurata sempre più complessa, immersiva e ritmica. Sul piano metodologico, il corpus assume come principio guida il “banale aristotelico”: partire esclusivamente da ciò che nel dipinto è visibile, misurabile e geometricamente controllabile, senza ricorrere a simbologie arbitrarie, geometrie occulte o sovrastrutture interpretative non falsificabili. Il metodo combina osservazione diretta delle tracce figurative, geometria inversa, retro-ingegneria CAD e verifiche di coerenza antropometrica, zoometrica e architettonica; il punto decisivo è che gli elementi pittorici — bugne

summary: Complete computational pipeline and outputs for the manuscript “Information limits of acoustic constraint on CO₂-mixture equations of state in the metering-critical window” (R. C. Aiken; prepared for Measurement Science and Technology). An earlier version of the manuscript was titled “Acoustically optimal state points for constraining CCS mixture models in the metering-critical region of CO₂ + N₂, O₂, and Ar”. Contents: candidate-grid Jacobians and input-derivative grids for CO₂ + N₂, O₂ and Ar (295–310 K, 7.4–11 MPa, 1–5 mol%); measurement designs with per-point precision requirements; projected covariances; replicate fit results; extracted literature comparison values; and the verified CO₂–Ar model implementation. The environment specification gives exact package versions and random seeds (CoolProp 8.0.0). New in version 1.2.0: Nested design sequences regenerated with a deterministic pair-search initialization. The 48-point designs are unchanged; the v1.1.0 sequences are retained as greedy_seq_v1_*.csv. Revision analyses (scripts/revision_*.py, outputs in out/revision/): dependence on composition uncertainty, comparison with conventional designs, batch structure, D/I/G criterion comparison, prediction uncertainty under parameter anchoring, density and bubble-pressure propagation, linearized out-of-family detection, and nonlinear coverage. README_REVISION.txt describes the additions and their run order.
title: Data and analysis code for: Information limits of acoustic constraint on CO₂-mixture equations of state in the metering-critical window

summary: Oltre il Quadrato: La griglia 4:3 e la precisione architettonica nell’Adorazione dei Magi Il saggio propone un ribaltamento metodologico nell’analisi del disegno preparatorio per l’Adorazione dei Magi di Leonardo da Vinci conservato agli Uffizi. Superando la tesi tradizionale di una maglia prospettica a base quadrata, l’autore dimostra, attraverso l’uso di software CAD e tecniche di retro-ingegneria, come Leonardo abbia adottato una griglia di rettangoli in rapporto armonico 4:3. Questa scoperta non solo risolve storiche incongruenze visive — restituendo alle arcate delle scale la loro perfetta forma a tutto sesto coerente con la misura del “braccio fiorentino” — ma svela un’applicazione consapevole di geometrie legate al pentagono e alla sezione aurea. Il lavoro sottolinea il notevole rigore logico e matematico di Leonardo, trasformando quello che era ritenuto un errore prospettico in una sofisticata architettura della visione. L’analisi si sviluppa attraverso una sequenza di osservazioni visive direttamente leggibili sul foglio 436E, verifiche CAD e procedimenti di geometria inversa, concepiti come linee di evidenza indipendenti ma convergenti. Beyond the Square: The 4:3 Grid and Architectural Perfection in the Adoration of the Magi This study presents a methodological shift in the analysis of Leonardo da Vinci’s preparatory drawing for the Adoration of the Magi. Moving beyond the traditional assumption of a square based perspective grid, the author utilizes CAD software and reverse-engineering techniques to demonstrate Leonardo’s use of a rectangular grid with a 4:3 harmonic ratio. This discovery resolves long-standing visual inconsistencies, showing that the arches in the background regain their perfect semicircular form when aligned with this modularity, consistent with the Florentine braccio unit of measurement. Furthermore, the analysis reveals the deliberate application of pentagonal geometry and the Golden Ratio.   This research highlights Leonardo’s mathematical rigour, showing that what was previously perceived as a perspectival error is, in fact, a sophisticated architecture of vision.  The analysis unfolds through a sequence of direct visual observations readable on the Uffizi sheet, CAD-based verifications, and inverse procedures, conceived as independent yet convergent lines of evidence.  This study integrates direct visual evidence from Leonardo’s drawing with CAD-based verification and inverse geometric reasoning.   Keywords: Leonardo da Vinci, Adoration of the Magi, Perspective, 4:3 Grid, CAD Analysis, Florentine Braccio, Golden Ratio.
title: Leonardo's CAD - La Geometria Svelata / The Revealed Geometry (it/en)

QUANTUM COMPUTING FOR INVERSE DESIGN OF 4D MATERIALS FAMILY 12 / F056-F060 / THE OTHER SIDE OF THE RESEARCH MONOGRAPH Feng Cheng-en (33) x STARLI / White Rainbow Era Scientific status: Prospective nonclinical proposal. All diagrams are analytical synthetic illustrations. No quantum advantage, qualified device, biomedical treatment or patient recovery has been demonstrated. THE OTHER SIDE OF THE 4D MATERIALS RESEARCH An inverse design begins with a wish: a material should bend to a specific shape after a particular sequence of heat, light, solvent or magnetic stimuli. The wish is not evidence. A specimen has a history, a printer has a feature limit, and a camera can mistake a smooth silhouette for recovered function. In this notebook the research chain is followed from physical permission to constitutive model, to competing computational designs, to damaged and rejected specimens, and finally to a negative case that another laboratory can recreate. Five independent flagships supply different scientific questions. F056 concerns a constrained inverse map from target response to material recipe. F057 studies the discrete matching of material configuration with time-dependent target shapes. F058 forces mathematical topology into a printable connected solid. F059 asks whether prediction intervals survive new lots and measurement chains. F060 refuses to consider a design validated until printed output, failures, material loss and costs have been measured. Coupling them yields a useful research system only when their evidence contracts remain distinct. The source genealogy matters. The author-provided four-dimensional microrobotics research book gives a physical vocabulary for responsive structures, fatigue and fabrication. The independent BCI-stroke study gives a separate rationale for minimizing assistance and distinguishing device function from recovery after a device is removed. The forty-family blueprint identifies the F056-F060 lineage and emphasizes the hazard of an optimum that cannot be manufactured. No source proves that a quantum-designed microbot has restored human motor function. Five-stage parallel spacetime reasoning is the public name of the present research method. The first stage asks what material and laboratory can legitimately do. The second asks which mathematical program is meaningful. The third proposes a strong ordinary rival. The fourth tries hard, bounded counterexamples. The fifth freezes the evidence that can survive independent reconstruction. This is a set of epistemic viewpoints, not a claim about physical parallel universes. A strong scientific notebook should be able to disagree with the monograph. Where the monograph records an observable and a pre-registered test, the notebook should ask why the observable was chosen, what the test would miss, and which apparently trivial rival might explain its result. Repetition can be a conceptual return to a difficult distinction rather than duplicated filler. But no return should be mistaken for new measurement. The most important distinction is between speed of design and quality of evidence. More candidate samples, more attractive plots or more pages cannot establish physical printability. Nor can a verified specimen establish quantum computational advantage if the full pipeline costs and carefully tuned classical methods were never compared. A scientific stop is legitimate when the boundary and next decisive experiment are clear. Research Doors should remain the most alive part of this system. The question left at the end of each chapter is not an invitation to endorse the current model. It is an instruction to try to defeat it with a better observation. If the next laboratory discovers that a classical algorithm, a clamp motion or a material batch artifact explains the beautiful result, the research family has still preserved useful knowledge. That is what makes it a handoff rather than a claim of perfection. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F056 | Quantum-Assisted Inverse Design of 4D Biomedical Materials at the Limit This flagship examines coupled composition-to-actuation inverse mapping under fabrication constraints. The relevant physical endpoints are held-out curvature error [1/m], tip displacement [um] and batch yield [1]. Its strongest immediate rival is the proposition that a rich surrogate or uncounted classical preprocessing explains the optimization gain. A blinded test should blindly swap material lots and stimulus order after designs are frozen. Independent instruments include independent optical displacement [um], curvature [1/m], locally mapped temperature [K], material lot ID and complete query ledger; the ordinary comparator set comprises tuned Bayesian optimization, adjoint or surrogate inverse search, classical mixed-integer programming and matched evaluation budgets. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a sequence across optimization, coding, topology, uncertainty and fabrication without importing one another's evidence. F057 | Quantum Material Configuration Search for Target Deformation at the Limit This flagship examines discrete formulation and voxel assignment search for target time-dependent deformation. The relevant physical endpoints are dynamic target mismatch [um] and valid-configuration ratio [1]. Its strongest immediate rival is the proposition that a simple classical lookup or favorable target selection explains the match. A blinded test should conceal target shapes and reverse their temporal stimulus order. Independent instruments include three-axis shape field [um], synchronized stimulus onset [s], printed voxel map and decoded composition identity; the ordinary comparator set comprises strong integer programming, genetic search, Bayesian optimization and conventional discrete trajectory matching under identical material alphabets. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a sequence across optimization, coding, topology, uncertainty and fabrication without importing one another's evidence. F058 | Quantum-Assisted Topology Optimization of 4D Microstructures at the Limit This flagship examines printable topology design under minimum-feature and connectivity constraints. The relevant physical endpoints are fabricated topology fidelity [1], stiffness [Pa] and actual curvature [1/m]. Its strongest immediate rival is the proposition that simulation favors disconnected or sub-resolution ligaments that cannot print. A blinded test should blindly print held-out topologies with fixed voxel resolution and support rules. Independent instruments include volumetric z-stack [um], print line width [um], calibrated microforce [uN], FE mesh ledger and connected-component count; the ordinary comparator set comprises calibrated SIMP, compliant-mechanism topology optimization, integer programming and mesh-matched density methods. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a sequence across optimization, coding, topology, uncertainty and fabrication without importing one another's evidence. F059 | Uncertainty Propagation in Quantum-Assisted Material Design at the Limit This flagship examines joint propagation of process, stimulus and inferred constitutive uncertainty. The relevant physical endpoints are predictive coverage [1], calibration error [um] and variance by material lot. Its strongest immediate rival is the proposition that surrogate uncertainty is underdispersed or repeated specimens are treated as independent. A blinded test should blindly challenge unseen lots at changed humidity, exposure and measurement chains. Independent instruments include held-out batch curvature [1/m], interval coverage [1], calibration-camera uncertainty [um] and independent lot identifiers; the ordinary comparator set comprises validated Monte Carlo, hierarchical uncertainty propagation, conformal calibration and independent classical surrogate models. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a sequence across optimization, coding, topology, uncertainty and fabrication without importing one another's evidence. F060 | Manufacturability and Experimental Validation of Quantum-Designed 4D Materials at the Limit This flagship examines closing the optimization-fabrication-test loop with hard defect and exposure vetoes. The relevant physical endpoints are print yield [1], metrology deviation [um], force drift [N] and full system cost. Its strongest immediate rival is the proposition that a virtual optimum disappears when sacrificial structures, curing and failed prints are counted. A blinded test should preregister fabrication quotas and independently measure every successful and failed specimen. Independent instruments include full attempted print roster, geometry residual [um], released particle mass [ug], force after cycling [uN] and cost ledger; the ordinary comparator set comprises a tuned classical design-of-experiments pipeline, matched-printer fabrication quota, process-cost accounting and blind metrology. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a sequence across optimization, coding, topology, uncertainty and fabrication without importing one another's evidence.

The independent BCI-stroke study gives a separate rationale for minimizing assistance and distinguishing device function from recovery after a device is removed. No source proves that a quantum-designed microbot has restored human motor function. Five-stage parallel spacetime reasoning is the public name of the present research method. No patient trial, tested quantum supremacy, demonstrated stroke recovery, or qualified medical device is claimed. THE OTHER SIDE OF THE CONTROL MONOGRAPH The technical notebook is not a glossary pasted below the research monograph. It is a second argumentative surface. The monograph states exactly what can be tested, with candidate equations, independent measurements and research gates. The notebook asks why the experiment deserves construction, which competing explanation should be taken most seriously and how an unsuccessful first generation could become a stronger foundation for someone else. This difference is a methodological commitment rather than a claim of novel experimental results. Family eleven begins from an uncomfortable contrast between optimization and authority. A method may compute a more attractive control input, but no numerical attractiveness can authorize an illegal actuator command. The physical and ethical permission envelope must be defined outside the optimizer, and a safe fallback must remain available when the proposed method is late, uncertain, energy-depleted or dependent on inaccessible backend infrastructure. The most important output of a difficult trial may be an unambiguous refusal. The five flagship mechanisms form a causal chain without becoming duplicates. F051 asks what it means to optimize permitted control gains fairly. F052 places the optimizer inside the receding-horizon control clock. F053 asks whether progressively less assistance can maintain a fixed mechanical task, while refusing to equate phantom success with human recovery. F054 requires energy and latency to be counted across acquisition, computation, communication and actuation. F055 tests whether every scientific conclusion remains subordinate to command legality, independent vetoes and serious classical rivals. This lineage comes from two distinct source studies and the author-supplied STARLI forty-family research DNA blueprint. The four-dimensional microrobotics source supplies material history, force generation, responsive structures and safety concerns. The BCI-stroke atlas supplies intention observability, minimally necessary assistance, withdrawal and the crucial distinction between assisted motion and restored independent function. These source relationships are not evidence that a fused 4D, quantum, BCI and clinical treatment platform exists. Five-stage parallel spacetime reasoning is a public name for a disciplined research workflow. Physical origin asks what the bench is permitted to do. Mathematical evolution asks which candidate model and parameters represent it. Counterfactual branching makes the ordinary baseline and hidden confounder genuine competitors. Extreme extrapolation applies bounded adversarial inputs, where the correct output may be stop. Evidence convergence leaves both a reconstructable result and an open Research Gate. These stages are viewpoints on one research contract, not literal physical parallel worlds. A 4D actuator can return to its familiar geometry and still lose force. A quantum optimizer can return a lower cost and still arrive after the legal deadline. A minimally assisted movement can succeed while a person would remain dependent on the device. A smooth average can hide a rare illegal command. Those four asymmetries explain why this research must separate shape, computation, mechanical assistance, function and safety, and why none of these outcomes can be imported into the others without a new experiment. The wisdom of stopping is the opposite of indifference. It means ending a research round when the testable contract is complete, the strongest rival has been confronted, the permission gates have been audited and the next laboratory can reconstruct the adverse case. When further parameter search no longer distinguishes the mechanism from the rival, additional polished prose or training calls do not create new evidence. The unresolved difference becomes an explicit research door for future investigators. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP RESEARCH CONTRACTS F051 | Quantum-Assisted Post-Stroke Rehabilitation Control Optimization at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is control gain search under hard actuator and state constraints. Its measurable endpoint is angle tracking error and total tuning-to-command cost. The leading alternative says benefit is produced by extra search, hidden preprocessing or the classical controller. The preregistered blind competition would blind-swap candidate gain vectors on identical nonhuman control traces. A fully observed test requires encoder angle [rad], actuator command, output torque [N m], motor work [J], gain-search calls and full wall time [ms] and resource-equivalent comparison with tuned robust PID/LQR, constrained SQP, CMA-ES and mixed-integer gain search with identical runs and CPU/GPU ledger. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question. F052 | Quantum-Assisted Model Predictive Control for Rehabilitation Robots at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is finite-horizon constrained optimization with receding-horizon deadlines. Its measurable endpoint is closed-loop error, solver completion percentile and deadline violation. The leading alternative says a solver-only benchmark ignores compilation, upload, readout and communication. The preregistered blind competition would conceal horizon changes and impose actuator-relevant controller deadlines. A fully observed test requires state estimator [rad,rad/s], solver input/output timestamp [ms], horizon [steps], safety margin and fallback event and resource-equivalent comparison with well-tuned conventional MPC, SQP, mixed-integer solvers, warm starts and robust tube MPC on identical task clocks. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question. F053 | Quantum Optimization for Minimum Necessary Assistance at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is assistance-minimizing policy with a fixed task-feasibility envelope. Its measurable endpoint is minimum delivered force and unassisted phantom-task feasibility. The leading alternative says a more forceful actuator makes the task look easier without reducing dependence. The preregistered blind competition would blindly taper physical assistance and test device-off task feasibility. A fully observed test requires independent load cell [N], motion target error [rad], assisted/unassisted phantom condition and residual passive force and resource-equivalent comparison with a fixed-gain assistive policy, optimal classical assistance scheduler and a fully disengaged zero-assistance phantom control. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question. F054 | Energy-Latency Tradeoffs in Quantum Rehabilitation Control at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is energy-constrained compute-actuation scheduling and deadline-aware fallback. Its measurable endpoint is joules per safe episode, wall latency and feasible trajectory fraction. The leading alternative says external service electricity or device idle consumption disappears from cost. The preregistered blind competition would inject finite battery, network stalls and safe-stop events in randomized order. A fully observed test requires electrical energy [J], power [W], battery state [J], acquisition and network timestamp [ms], safe-stop trace and resource-equivalent comparison with energy-aware classical MPC, local deterministic fallback and measured on-device scheduling with the same task energy budget. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question. F055 | Safety-Constrained Quantum Rehabilitation Control Against Classical Baselines at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is noncompensatory command legality with paired quantum-classical evaluation. Its measurable endpoint is illegal commands, veto timing, safety margin and matched-cost task error. The leading alternative says rare forbidden states are omitted while average performance improves. The preregistered blind competition would inject hidden infeasible states and verify fail-silent refusal before actuation. A fully observed test requires command legality indicator, independent hardware veto timestamp [ms], state margin, source version and paired baseline results and resource-equivalent comparison with independently certified physical interlock, robust classical MPC, rule-based veto and cost-matched quantum candidates. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question.

summary: Replication package for the paper "Percentile in Percentile: Evaluating Scholars Across Career Stages" (Ipeirotis & Tian, Quantitative Science Studies). Contents: the SQL that builds every table in the paper ( sql/ , numbered in run order); CSV exports of the 28 result tables those queries write, aggregates only ( results/ ); the data behind every figure and the plotting scripts ( figures/ ); the Lean 4 formal verification package ( lean/ ) and numerical checks ( checks/ ) of the score's properties; the curated Wikidata honors and the scripts of the later-recognition test ( honors/ ); the manuscript source ( manuscript_qss/ ); COMPUTATION.md , which explains how the SQL evaluates the integral that defines PiP; and FINDINGS.md , which records every number with the query that produced it. The per-author and per-article tables (about 312 GB, and 215 GB for the analysis without self-citations) are not in this archive. They are in the BigQuery datasets scholar-version2.paper_rp and scholar-version2.paper_rp_noself , which anyone signed in to Google Cloud can query; queries are billed to the reader's own project. Sources: Semantic Scholar Academic Graph, release 2026-10-27 (ODC-BY); Wikidata (CC0), queried 5 November 2026. An interactive demonstration of the metric on Google Scholar profiles is available at pip-score.org , and author-level statistics for the Google Scholar profiles can be downloaded from pip-score.org/data ; for legal reasons (Google Scholar's terms of service), raw per-article data from Google Scholar profiles cannot be made openly available.
title: Replication package for "Percentile in Percentile: Evaluating Scholars Across Career Stages"

summary: Many high-stakes AI failures trace to the training data rather than the model, yet teams still treat pre-training data validation as a checklist and rarely wire its signals to a go/no-go decision or to a governance framework. We study the detectability boundary of that validation: what a pre-training data-readiness gate catches, what it misses, and why a flagged source is often not blocked. We reuse a validation gate from a prior single-domain system and generalize it across three high-stakes domains (healthcare, finance, and government) on the real MIMIC-IV, SEC EDGAR, and CMS Open Payments datasets, injecting controlled defects across simulated sources. A composite readiness score detects 0.76 of degraded sources (95% CI [0.74, 0.76]) but withholds only 0.42; the 0.34 gap (95% CI [0.32, 0.35]) traces to a single averaging step, and we show it is fixable but privacy-sensitive. The grid is small by design (six sources per domain, two degraded, five seeds), so the intervals describe this controlled setting, not field variability. We map the privacy-utility curve of validating on differentially private summaries, prove a blind spot for symmetric label noise on balanced targets, and add a confident-learning label detector that runs on DP-noised summaries and keeps its recall down to epsilon = 0.1. We compare against Great Expectations and Deequ, measure how poorly thresholds port across domains, and map the gate to the NIST AI RMF MEASURE function. We report the negatives, among them a near-chance inter-rater reliability on fine-grained incident coding. What is new is the integration of production incidents, a private benchmarked gate, and a governance mapping, not any one of those parts.

summary: siwecal-soft v0.1.0 First release of siwecal-soft , the software of the SiW-ECAL TB2026 test-beam campaign at CERN: data conversion, simulation, reconstruction and analysis in one Key4hep/Gaudi project. Origin This repository merges two earlier repositories into a single code base with a fresh history: siwecal_k4sim @ 075dedd : simulation of the prototype. DD4hep geometry (including the H2-like upstream beam line), ddsim launchers, digitisation and the simulation campaigns. siwecal-tb2026 @ 90b2e55 : test-beam data. Raw/LCIO decoding, event building with the muon calibration, particle-ID shower variables, ACTS tracking, event viewer and analysis. An important part of the DAQ data decoding (SLB frame and raw decoders) and of the pedestal/MIP calibration is based on SiWECAL-TB-analysis , the SiW-ECAL test-beam analysis software. Both repositories are frozen at those commits (tag final-before-monorepo ); new development happens here. Every file of the two repositories is accounted for in tools/migration/ (copied, rewritten or excluded), and the merge was validated against the frozen builds (identical tracking output: 137/137 data and 144/144 simulation EDM4hep branches). What changed with the merge One CMake project (C++20, Key4hep 2026-04-08), one install, one environment script ( init_siwecalsoft.sh ). Shared code and mappings live once in common/ ; calibration tables are read from EOS only. Unified ACTS tracking for data and simulation. Processing steps formerly done in Python now run as Gaudi algorithms: ecal tree writer, occupancy-sag and trigger turn-on calibrators, and the post-PID event selection and valtree ( EcalEventSelection , EcalValTreeWriter ). Each was validated against the Python version. New: run-by-run simulation ( simulation/campaign/make_run_sim_dag.py ). One simulated sample per data run, with the gun tuned to that run's measured beam spot ( siwecal_beamspot ) and the run's statistics; used for final_v10. Control tests ( tests/control/ ) run with ./build.sh (ctest + pytest). Authors Jesus Pedro Marquez Hernandez (IJCLab), Olmo Arquero Peinazo (CIEMAT), Yukun Shi (LLR). See CITATION.cff for how to cite this software.
title: siwecal-soft: SiW-ECAL TB2026 data conversion, simulation and analysis software

summary: 🧬 Streptococcus iniae SIKU01 — Genome, Comparative Genomics and Reverse Vaccinology Release: Manuscript v43 · 26 October 2026 Response to reviewers (peer-review round 1): RESPONSE_TO_REVIEWERS_v43 · 26 October 2026 📖 Overview This repository provides the genome assembly, comparative genomic datasets, analysis code, vaccine-candidate prioritization results, and supporting reproducibility resources for Streptococcus iniae strain SIKU01. Five S. iniae isolates (SIKU01–SIKU05) were obtained from diseased farmed Asian seabass ( Lates calcarifer ) in Thailand and sequenced using Illumina paired-end technology. The SIKU01 dataset was selected for complete genome assembly and annotation. The study integrates genome annotation, comparative genomics across 90 S. iniae isolates, pangenome and conservation analyses, antigen characterization, reverse vaccinology, and Quality-by-Design (QbD) approaches to prioritize candidates according to immunological and biomanufacturing criteria. 🔗 Public sequence records Resource Accession / link NCBI BioProject PRJNA933632 SIKU01 BioSample SAMN33244440 SIKU01 GenBank chromosome CP121692.1 GenBank assembly GCA_046581345.1 RefSeq assembly GCF_046581345.1 SIKU01 raw reads SRR23406918 Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.22128864 Zenodo all-versions citation 10.5281/zenodo.15264953 🧫 Raw sequencing datasets Five Illumina paired-end sequencing datasets were deposited under BioProject PRJNA933632. Five S. iniae isolates (SIKU01–SIKU05) were obtained from diseased farmed Asian seabass ( Lates calcarifer ) in Thailand and sequenced using Illumina paired-end technology. The SIKU01 dataset was selected for complete genome assembly and annotation. The study integrates genome annotation, comparative genomics across 90 S. iniae isolates, pangenome and conservation analyses, antigen characterization, reverse vaccinology, and Quality-by-Design (QbD) approaches to prioritize candidates according to immunological and biomanufacturing criteria. 🔗 Public sequence records Resource Accession / link NCBI BioProject PRJNA933632 SIKU01 BioSample SAMN33244440 SIKU01 GenBank chromosome CP121692.1 GenBank assembly GCA_046581345.1 RefSeq assembly GCF_046581345.1 SIKU01 raw reads SRR23406918 Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.22128864 Zenodo all-versions citation 10.5281/zenodo.15264953 🧫 Raw sequencing datasets Five Illumina paired-end sequencing datasets were deposited under BioProject PRJNA933632. Isolate NCBI SRA accession SIKU01 SRR23406918 SIKU02 SRR23406921 SIKU03 SRR23406920 SIKU04 SRR23406919 SIKU05 SRR23406922 The public complete genome assembly and annotation correspond to SIKU01. The remaining four sequencing datasets are retained as raw sequencing records. 📦 Files included in this dataset 📝 Manuscript File Description 01_Manuscript_RV_SI_v43.pdf Manuscript, PDF format 01_Manuscript_RV_SI_v43.docx Editable Word manuscript 01_Manuscript_RV_SI_v43_corrected.md Markdown manuscript source, including six embedded figures 📊 Data workbooks Each workbook includes a CONTENTS sheet describing its tables and supporting metadata. summary: Split Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) compression data for 22 AISI 316 stainless steel specimens: raw bar signals, processed 1-wave / 3-wave stress-strain series, and the specimen and test records (RDF/Turtle, QUDT units, W3C PROV. From these tests: Johnson-Cook and Zerilli-Armstrong calibrations by least-squares fit and by a physics-informed neural network (PINN) - 78 single-seed runs and 8 seed ensembles, with parameter cards, uncertainties, identifiability diagnostics, training logs, predicted stress surfaces and checkpoints - and 308 LS-DYNA simulations of the tests driven by the calibrated models. See README.md for the layout and data_dictionary.csv for every term and column.
title: SS316L dynamic compression: SHPB tests, LS-DYNA simulations and physics-informed constitutive calibrations

summary: Observed Palworld stat values support the Palworld IV formula and its modifiers: a binary32 passive percent round trip, food-rate corrections, hunger, party bonuses that replace specific Attack Up and Defense Up passives, emblem bonuses, partner star ladders, linear helper contributions and maximum-only same-species source stacking. This dataset accompanies Lore Armory's v3.1 technical note. The full CSV contains 2,594 checked values, including 272 older contextual rows outside the note's 2,322-value denominator; 194 of the note's values are screenshot-backed readings from worlds L and L3. Frozen numerical predictions, competing alternatives and later eligibility corrections are kept distinct, and public mathematical copies of the frozen prediction sheets carry their own checksums, separate from the original commitments (the superseded J v1 sheet stays marked as such). Screenshot references and hashes accompany the readback ledger. The README supplies column definitions, exact count filters, observation provenance and open questions. The archive iv-data-v3.1.tar.gz holds the full data directory with its folder structure. The package does not claim confirmation of enhancement statuses, combat-only conditional effects or tower-boss HP scaling.
title: Palworld Pal stat verification: observations and frozen predictions (v3.1)

summary: This record contains supplementary research materials supporting the manuscript entitled "Evaluating Out-of-Fold Weighted Soft Voting for Network Intrusion Detection: Benefits and Limitations of Classifier Fusion" (Manuscript ID: MJCSC-D-26-00018R3), submitted to the Mesopotamian Journal of Computer Science. The study evaluates training-derived optimized weighted soft voting for multiclass network intrusion detection using Decision Tree (DT-Gini), Random Forest variants (RF-Gini and RF-Entropy), and XGBoost. The primary evaluation uses a prepared CICIDS2017 development subset comprising 78,437 observations and 15 traffic classes. An additional dataset-specific evaluation uses a prepared CICIoT2023 subset comprising 99,327 observations, 34 traffic classes, and 39 numerical predictors. The experimental framework includes data preprocessing, mutual information-based feature selection, training-only minority-class oversampling, stratified outer cross-validation, and inner out-of-fold optimization of classifier fusion weights. The supplementary materials are intended to support verification of the reported experimental configurations and results. The original complete source-scanning log and sampling-run metadata for CICIoT2023 are unavailable; therefore, exact independent reconstruction of the original sampling run has not been established. These materials accompany the third-round revised manuscript submitted to the journal.

summary: This paper studies all-to-all broadcast scheduling for underwater swarms with collision-resilient physical layers that can decode asynchronously overlapping packets. Propagation-aware collision-free schedulers coordinate packet arrivals but do not account for this reception capability. We first design a data-driven neural reception model that captures per-interferer power and timing effects. The model improves prediction accuracy over SINR baselines while admitting an exact mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation. The resulting neural-network-embedded MILP (NN-MILP) optimizes transmission times while explicitly encoding schedule-dependent overlaps and the predictor's inference, enabling globally optimal scheduling for small-scale instances. For larger networks, a two-stage ant colony optimization (ACO) heuristic combines low-cost transmission-order search with neural-aware timing refinement. Simulation results show that ACO shortens broadcast rounds compared with existing schedulers. It approaches the NN-MILP optimum on small-scale instances while supporting larger networks at substantially lower computational cost.
title: Collision-Resilient All-to-All Broadcast Scheduling in Underwater Acoustic Networks

summary: Accurate future channel state information (CSI) is essential for underwater acoustic (UWA) communication because delays associated with signal propagation, feedback, scheduling, and transceiver reconfiguration can render currently available CSI outdated. However, most existing predictors estimate only the next channel state and obtain multi-step forecasts through recursive rollout, which causes prediction errors to accumulate as the multipath structure evolves. The scarcity of sea-trial measurements further limits reliable model training. To address these challenges, we propose LLM4UACP, a dual-domain, structure-preserving framework that adapts a pretrained Transformer for few-shot multi-step UWA channel prediction. LLM4UACP extracts complementary features from the channel impulse response (CIR) and channel frequency response (CFR), aligns them through Fourier-consistent fusion, and encodes the fused representation as delay-time tokens. A pretrained Transformer with a frozen backbone is adapted through Butterfly Orthogonal Fine-tuning to jointly predict multiple future CIRs in a single forward pass, thereby avoiding the error accumulation associated with recursive prediction. Experiments on the measured SO-06 and SO-07 channels show that LLM4UACP achieves normalized mean squared error (NMSE) values of 0.0411 and 0.0399, corresponding to reductions of 88.53% and 85.15%, respectively, relative to the most recent baseline. With only 0.11M trainable parameters, LLM4UACP maintains robust performance across varying prediction horizons and observation-window lengths, limited-data settings, and cross-dataset transfer scenarios.
title: Multi-Step Underwater Acoustic Channel Prediction via Dual-Domain Structure Preservation and Pretrained Transformer

However, most existing predictors estimate only the next channel state and obtain multi-step forecasts through recursive rollout, which causes prediction errors to accumulate as the multipath structure evolves. The scarcity of sea-trial measurements further limits reliable model training. To address these challenges, we propose LLM4UACP, a dual-domain, structure-preserving framework that adapts a pretrained Transformer for few-shot multi-step UWA channel prediction. LLM4UACP extracts complementary features from the channel impulse response (CIR) and channel frequency response (CFR), aligns them through Fourier-consistent fusion, and encodes the fused representation as delay-time tokens. A pretrained Transformer with a frozen backbone is adapted through Butterfly Orthogonal Fine-tuning to jointly predict multiple future CIRs in a single forward pass, thereby avoiding the error accumulation associated with recursive prediction. Experiments on the measured SO-06 and SO-07 channels show that LLM4UACP achieves normalized mean squared error (NMSE) values of 0.0411 and 0.0399, corresponding to reductions of 88.53% and 85.15%, respectively, relative to the most recent baseline. With only 0.11M trainable parameters, LLM4UACP maintains robust performance across varying prediction horizons and observation-window lengths, limited-data settings, and cross-dataset transfer scenarios.

summary: Grid mismatch in wideband channel estimation leaves structured cancellation residuals after strong-path subtraction. These residuals generate spurious correlation peaks or mask weak arrivals, turning continuous parameter errors into path-count errors. We propose RC-SAGE-Brent, a residual-closed-loop estimator that jointly refines continuous delay-scale parameters and corrects the unknown-order path set. Within each feedback cycle, ambiguity-constrained alternating Brent searches suppress strong-path cancellation residuals. Candidate validation, resolution-constrained pruning, and full-domain residual redetection then revise the active path set. For linear frequency modulation (LFM) probes, an observable signal-to-residual ratio adaptively scales the model-order penalty to mitigate overestimation caused by delay-scale coupling. Theoretical analysis links off-grid parameter errors to local cancellation-residual curvature and weak-path detectability. Factorial ablations, paired comparisons against standard sparse and off-grid estimators, and measured channel replay demonstrate improved path-set recovery and waveform reconstruction while delineating the operational boundaries of the method.
title: Residual-Closed-Loop SAGE-Brent Estimation for Unknown-Order Wideband Underwater Acoustic Channels

summary: The proliferation of maritime activities has spurred the emergence of numerous computation-intensive and delay-sensitive marine applications and services. Given the inherent rationality, selfish nature, and limited computational abilities of marine devices, devising effective strategies to incentivize their participation in task processing become a critical challenge. In this paper, we investigate the satellite-assisted marine multi-access edge computing (MEC) and propose a two-tier task offloading scheme through a hybrid Stackelberg-Bargaining game approach to enhance offloading efficiency and maximize the utility of marine devices. Specifically, for the underwater acoustic communication, we consider the scenario where multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), managed by maritime autonomous surface ships (MASSs), upload their collected data using non-orthogonal multiple access(NOMA) to optimize channel utilization. For the data transmission above the sea surface, we consider the scenario where a low earth orbit satellite (LEOS) functions as a space edge server to provide computing services, and MASS offloads workloads to LEOS through frequency division multiple access(FDMA) to prevent co-channel interference. we define the utility of AUVs, MASSs and LEOSs, and model the offloading process between AUVs and MASSs as a Stackelberg game, while representing the offloading interaction between MASSs and LEOSs as a Bargaining game. Additionally, we propose efficient algorithms to optimize AUV offloading strategies and MASS pricing strategies, while refining the bidding strategies for both MASSs and LEOSs. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithms significantly outperform benchmark schemes in achieving optimal solutions.

summary: Underwater acoustic communication faces challenges such as limited available bandwidth and complex channel environments, which impose demanding requirements on efficient image transmission and reliable reconstruction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a generative image communication framework based on cross-modal semantic successive refinement. At the transmitter, text descriptions, compact bottleneck features, and visual side information compressed by residual vector quantization are transmitted. At the receiver, text and bottleneck features are first fused to predict a base estimate of the intermediate visual representation. The received RVQ indices are then used to recover supplementary visual information and perform residual correction, followed by image reconstruction using a one-step Pixel Mean Flow model. During training, a CLIP-based text-image semantic consistency constraint is introduced to preserve the semantic correspondence between generated results and the original text descriptions. During transmission, protection resources are allocated according to the importance of different information branches and RVQ quantization stages. Simulations using COCO 2017 images and measured underwater acoustic channel records from Watermark show that text and bottleneck features provide complementary semantic and structural conditions, RVQ visual side information further improves reconstruction quality, and layered unequal error protection helps improve recovery at low SNRs. Code-rate allocation experiments reveal a tradeoff between the reliability of fundamental conditions and visual-detail reconstruction under a limited visual-feature coding budget, providing guidance for allocating protection resources in underwater acoustic image transmission.
title: Cross-Modal Semantic Successive Refinement for Generative Image Communication over Underwater Acoustic Channels

summary: Acoustic holography in the megahertz range can impact applications from manufacturing and non-destructive testing to transcranial ultrasound. Designing lens topologies for complex holograms in the sub-megahertz to low-megahertz regime most relevant to transcranial therapy is difficult because wave propagation through an acoustically thick lens cannot be ignored. Here we show that the heterogeneous angular spectrum approach (HASA), which admits in-plane varying speed-of-sound maps and supports rapid differentiable optimization with the Adam optimizer, can generate three-dimensional lens topologies directly. With it we quantify the failure of the thin-element approximation (TEA) at these frequencies, where lenses enter an acoustically thick regime (thickness L much greater than the wavelength) governed by refractive walk-off, and we introduce a dimensionless refractive walk-off number Nw that defines a frequency-dependent operating regime. Topology optimization outperformed TEA-based design in all 45 configurations tested, with the largest structural gains at or below 1 MHz; for high-numerical-aperture designs the fidelity at 1 MHz matched that at 2 MHz, while structural similarity was highest at 0.5 MHz. The sub-megahertz to low-megahertz window is therefore a favorable operating regime for high-fidelity transcranial holography rather than one to be avoided. Free-field hydrophone measurements of 3D-printed lenses reproduced the designed patterns, and because the framework also accounts for aberration in heterogeneous media, patient-specific lenses corrected skull-induced aberration in simulation and ex vivo experiment, generalized across skull segments, and shaped volumetric beams through the human skull. Together these results provide a framework for designing simple, economical, and high-performance ultrasound systems.

summary: We propose a Raspberry Pi-based underwater vessel classification system for edge deployment under limited connectivity, bandwidth and power in offshore acoustic surveillance. Using ShipsEar, we compare six classifiers on a Raspberry Pi 5 through a complete audio-to-prediction pipeline. We assess classification performance, processing latency, CPU utilisation, memory consumption and monitored power. Supporting experiments examine acoustic feature selection, statistical pooling and Transformer patch configurations. The two-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) achieved a mean macro-F1 of \textbf{(99.14 \textpm{} 0.32)\%} across five random seeds. The radial basis function support vector machine (RBF-SVM) achieved \textbf{98.83\%}, with a median end-to-end latency of 28.109~ms compared with 120.655~ms for the CNN. This favourable trade-off motivated RBF-SVM deployment on the Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W. It maintained the same classification performance with a median end-to-end latency of \textbf{349.09~ms} and a sustained throughput of \textbf{2.962 classifications/s}, or \textbf{14.8} times the rate required for consecutive five-second audio segments.
title: Lightweight Underwater Acoustic Vessel Classification for Embedded Deployment

summary: Underwater acoustic passive detection is essential to maritime surveillance and intelligent ocean sensing. Existing detection systems typically collapse multichannel array observations into a binary decision or a scalar confidence score, offering limited insight into the physical evidence that supports or contradicts a target declaration. This limitation is acute at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), where isolated spectral peaks and transient beamforming responses are inherently ambiguous and physically verifiable targets are characterized by an ensemble of coupled reinforcing cues. Building on the unified from-signals-to-evidence framework introduced in the companion Part I, this paper instantiates the framework for passive target detection. A physics-aware multichannel acoustic encoder encodes the array observations into complementary acoustic evidence tokens through a direction-guided architecture that combines minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) processing with time-frequency and fine-frequency representations. These tokens are combined with environmental priors and fed into a pretrained large language model (LLM) that evaluates target-present and noise-only hypotheses and generates a structured detection report detailing target presence, bearing, spectral-line locations, received SNR, range, and per-field confidence scores. A physics-parameterized data engine extended to realistic oceanic channels provides traceable supervision at both discrete-label and structured-description levels. Experiments under white-noise and mixed ocean-background conditions demonstrate reliable detection, accurate bearing estimation, and physically interpretable structured reports, validating the feasibility of evidence-grounded underwater acoustic detection.
title: From Signals to Evidence: Interpretable Underwater Acoustic Target Sensing with Large Language Models - Part II: Passive Detection

This limitation is acute at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), where isolated spectral peaks and transient beamforming responses are inherently ambiguous and physically verifiable targets are characterized by an ensemble of coupled reinforcing cues. Building on the unified from-signals-to-evidence framework introduced in the companion Part I, this paper instantiates the framework for passive target detection. A physics-aware multichannel acoustic encoder encodes the array observations into complementary acoustic evidence tokens through a direction-guided architecture that combines minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) processing with time-frequency and fine-frequency representations. These tokens are combined with environmental priors and fed into a pretrained large language model (LLM) that evaluates target-present and noise-only hypotheses and generates a structured detection report detailing target presence, bearing, spectral-line locations, received SNR, range, and per-field confidence scores. A physics-parameterized data engine extended to realistic oceanic channels provides traceable supervision at both discrete-label and structured-description levels. Experiments under white-noise and mixed ocean-background conditions demonstrate reliable detection, accurate bearing estimation, and physically interpretable structured reports, validating the feasibility of evidence-grounded underwater acoustic detection.
